rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis uses mechanical loading (strain rate/temperature) to induce phase separation, while the target uses thermal aging to control ordering and phase boundary morphology. These are different kinds of interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies high strain rates and cryogenic/sub-ambient temperatures, whereas the target uses a specific thermal aging window (550-750°C). These are contradictory regimes.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis proposes stress-induced phase separation creating brittle phases, while the target describes L12 ordering, APBE increase, and jagged phase boundary stress concentration. These are different mechanisms.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts reduced toughness under demanding mechanical conditions, while the target predicts a non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition with temperature. The property (toughness/ductility) is the same, but the predicted pattern and direction differ.
